title: Final Value of Variable After Performing Operations
statement: A tiny language has a single variable `X`, which starts at `0`, and four statements: `"++X"` and `"X++"` each add 1 to `X`, while `"--X"` and `"X--"` each subtract 1 from it. Run the statements in `operations` from first to last and return the value `X` holds at the end.
notes:
## Intuition

Each statement moves `X` by exactly one step, up or down; whether the operator is written before or after `X` makes no difference here. In every one of the four strings the middle character is the operator's sign (`+` or `-`), so one character tells us the direction.

## Approach

1. Start with `x = 0`.
2. For each `operation`, look at its middle character `operation[1]`.
3. If it is `+`, add 1 to `x`; otherwise subtract 1.
4. Return `x` after the last statement.

## Example 1, step by step

`operations = ["--X","X++","X++"]`. `x` starts at `0`. `"--X"` has `-` in the middle, so `x = -1`. `"X++"` has `+` in the middle, so `x = 0`. The last `"X++"` makes `x = 1`, which is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time check per statement.
- Space: O(1): only the counter `x`.

## Pitfalls

- Checking only the first character fails for `"X++"` and `"X--"`, whose first character is `X`.
- Prefix and postfix forms behave the same here; there is no "value before the update" to return.
- The answer can be negative, down to `-100`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x` | the current value of the variable `X` |
| `operation` | the statement being run |

narration.3: Run the statements one at a time, in order.
narration.4: The middle character is the sign in all four forms; a plus means increment.
narration.7: Otherwise the statement decrements X by one.
narration.10: After the last statement, x holds the final value.
